questions.q: Which earlier chapter's identity pattern did Lesson 29's single conditional access policy, spanning on-prem and cloud, actually come from?
options: Chapter 6, Data Architecture
Chapter 2, Multi-Cloud Strategy
Chapter 4, Hybrid Identity
Chapter 7, Cost and Governance
questions.explain: Unifying identity and conditional access across on-prem and cloud environments is Chapter 4's contribution, applied directly in Lesson 29's design.

questions.q: Lesson 31's Brennick Retail case study is a direct illustration of the warning from which chapter?
options: Chapter 2, Multi-Cloud Strategy
Chapter 5, Multi-Cloud Networking
Chapter 1, Hybrid Fundamentals
Chapter 3, Workload Portability
questions.explain: Chapter 2 warned that multi-cloud adopted as a blanket policy without a per-workload cost model tends to cost more than it saves -- exactly what Brennick's story shows.

questions.q: What two tools from Chapter 3 did Lesson 30's deployment lab rely on directly?
options: The unified cost view and the FOCUS billing schema
The Kubernetes portability boundary (Lesson 9) and the multi-cloud Terraform module pattern (Lesson 11)
The conditional access policy and Azure AD Connect
The ExpressRoute circuit and the colocation meet-point
questions.explain: Lesson 30 directly reused Lesson 9's portable Deployment/Service core and Lesson 11's one-module-called-twice pattern to deploy identically to AKS and EKS.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what discipline does this capstone's two labs and one case study teach together, read as a whole?
options: That hybrid and multi-cloud architecture should always be avoided entirely
That every workload should be deployed to at least two clouds for safety
That cost modeling is unnecessary once an architecture has been designed
That hybrid and multi-cloud tools earn their cost only when a real, specific requirement drives the design -- not when reached for by default
questions.explain: Lessons 29-30 show deliberate, requirement-driven hybrid/multi-cloud design; Lesson 31 shows the cost of reaching for the same tools by default, with no requirement or cost model behind it.

questions.q: According to this lesson and lib/career-paths.ts, what are the other three Expert Specialization courses in this path, and in what order must they be taken relative to this course?
options: Advanced Platform Engineering/GitOps/CI-CD, AI Cloud Infrastructure/GPU Computing/MLOps, and Advanced SRE/Disaster Recovery/Resilience -- in any order, since none of the four Expert Specialization courses depend on each other
They must be taken in a strict sequence, starting with Advanced SRE
This course must be completed last, after all three other Expert Specialization courses
There are no other Expert Specialization courses in this path
questions.explain: All four Expert Specialization courses build on the Advanced Specialization stage but not on each other, so a student can take them in any order once that stage is complete.
